items.heading: Eating with hands
details: Ayurveda links the five fingers to the five elements - space, air, fire, water, and earth - believed to be balanced before food is eaten.
Touching food stimulates digestive juices through nerve endings in the fingertips, and fingers sense temperature before the mouth does, helping avoid burns.

items.heading: Sitting on the floor to eat (Sukhasana)
details: Sitting cross-legged is believed to activate the vagus nerve, signaling the brain that the stomach is filling and helping prevent overeating.
The posture improves blood circulation to the abdomen, aiding digestion.

items.heading: Rice and dal together
details: Cereals and legumes provide complementary amino-acid profiles, making the combination more nutritionally complete than either alone.

items.heading: Idli fermentation
details: Microbial fermentation changes the batter's texture, flavor, and digestibility before steaming.

items.heading: Dosa fermentation
details: Fermentation transforms the batter through beneficial microorganisms, improving flavor and nutrient availability.

items.heading: Curd / Dahi fermentation
details: Lactic-acid bacteria lower the pH of milk, which helps preserve it and adds beneficial probiotic cultures.

items.heading: Buttermilk / Chaas / Majiga
details: A light, diluted after-meal drink that provides hydration, nutrients, and potentially beneficial microorganisms.

items.heading: Sattu
details: A roasted and ground grain or pulse preparation that provides protein and other nutrients in a quick, convenient form.

items.heading: Indian spice combinations
details: Spice blends provide a wide diversity of phytochemicals, and several individual spices have antimicrobial properties.

items.heading: Turmeric in cooking
details: Provides curcuminoids and other biologically active compounds with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.

items.heading: Ginger in cooking
details: Contains bioactive compounds, with some evidence supporting its traditional use for nausea.

items.heading: Garlic in cooking
details: Contains biologically active sulfur compounds studied for a range of health effects.

items.heading: Chewing fennel seeds or paan after meals
details: Fennel and betel leaf are traditionally believed to aid digestion right after a meal.
Chewing increases saliva production, which helps further break down food, and spices like cloves and cardamom used in paan freshen the breath.
